extracted.intended_audience: readers of early-modern voyage accounts; historians and students of exploration/navigation
extracted.subtask_description: A primary-source narrative of a Pacific voyage (early modern Spanish exploration) describing navigation, encounters with island peoples, shipboard discipline, provisioning, and procedures for making discoveries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Navigation and charting accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for correct navigation and charting: do not rely solely on dead reckoning or multiply degrees incorrectly; calculate by estimated leagues and known latitude and account for errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the text: the Chief Pilot “multiplied degrees on the W.S.W. course… when it should have been, for more accuracy, by the estimated leagues and the known latitude.” He “did not calculate for errors in determining distances in a route from east to west, and their two quarters, caused by the variation of the needle, more or less leeway, winds and sails and other things to be considered.” Practical guidance: take sun observations to fix latitude, adjust dead reckoning for compass variation, leeway, wind and sail effects, and use estimated leagues rather than naive course-degree multiplication. The passage treats failure to do so as a substantive professional deficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pilot assembly and decision-making procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: When there is disagreement about position or course, convene a public counsel where each pilot states the number of leagues he believes they are from the port and gives his reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure described: hoist the flag signal for counsel, have pilots show their charts and notes, and require each to state in public his reckoning and justification. Use collective scrutiny (charts, notes, sun observations) to resolve differences and to calm unease among the crew.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach to unknown coasts and anchoring cautions
rubrics_metrics.description: Approach unknown shores cautiously: navigate at night under small sail, keep good lookouts, have lanterns lighted, send a launch/a boat ahead to reconnoitre, sound frequently, and keep anchors ready.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: “we therefore navigated at night under small sail, keeping a good look-out, the lanterns lighted, with the launch ahead, having orders to signal with lights if there were rocks or land.” When crossing shoals they were “always sounding, and with the anchors ready and look-out men at the mast-heads to report what they saw.” Practical anti-pattern: approaching unknown coasts with full sail, no sounding, or no reconnoitring launch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shipboard discipline and handling of mutiny or inefficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: The captain must enforce discipline, remove or restrain inefficient or ungrateful officers, and act decisively to prevent licence and disturbances among the crew.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrative guidance: the Captain removed the Chief Pilot for incompetence and quelled supporters; he later “caused a block to be placed at the yard-arm” and lived “with a caution necessary among such villains.” The account endorses decisive action (threats, removal, confinement) to maintain order and prevent internecine strife. It also records regret at not bringing irons/ fetters for enforcing discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of gambling; promote productive instruction and duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Discourage playing (gambling) and swearing aboard ship; instead promote educational and useful activities (reading, writing, arithmetic, military drill, fortification, artillery, navigation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Captain argued that “they would not risk to go on with such new and good work if there was playing and swearing” and preferred alms given without gambling. Suggested alternative pastimes: books, teaching reading/writing/counting, master-at-arms instruction, and teaching spheres and navigation. Anti-pattern: allowing gambling that undermines discipline and mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction with natives: conciliation, gifts, and religious rites
rubrics_metrics.description: Approach indigenous peoples with friendly gestures, gifts, and religious rites; attempt conciliation and introduction of the Christian faith where possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in the text: giving cloaks, sashes, dressing chiefs in fine cloth (“dressed him in shot silk”), kissing hands, performing Mass with natives present who imitated gestures, and valuing bells and trinkets in trade. The account explicitly notes the ease with which such peoples “would receive the Faith if there was any one to teach them.” Cautionary note: forcible seizure of natives can provoke distress and escape (seizures caused alarm and fugitives).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording discoveries and use of observations
rubrics_metrics.description: Record positions, bearings, and island names; use celestial observations (sun at sunrise/sunset, equinox) and compass bearings to determine latitude and variation, and keep logs of distances and local information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practices shown: observing needles at equinox and comparing sunrise/sunset, taking the sun to establish latitude (e.g., latitude 10° 20′), writing down native names and compass bearings of islands, and counting nights to indicate sailing time to other lands. Naming conventions and recording of latitudes/distances are treated as essential for corroboration and future navigation.
